summary: Edge SNI cache miss triggers cross-region TLS handshake retries and p99 spike
description:
Issue summary: Several of AtlasMail's streaming generation requests experienced prolonged connection setup times beginning 2026-03-12 02:10 UTC. Symptoms point to TLS/SNI handshake retries to a remote POP (eu-west) instead of the expected local POP (us-west), resulting in a sustained p99 token latency increase and occasional streaming disconnects.

Impact: Customer reports degraded user experience in production: long tail response times (p99 tokens ~4-6s additional), occasional streaming cancels, and an increase in erroring client sessions. Affects ~3% of their production traffic routed through the us-west edge for the last 48 hours.

Environment: Dedicated account on prod, us-west edge fronting, backend serving pool pinned to redwood-rr-medium. AtlasMail traffic pattern: many short streaming requests (avg 40 tokens), high connection churn.

Observed timeframe: 2026-03-12 02:10 UTC - ongoing (intermittent recurrences).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer API request from us-west region using streaming chat API with model redwood-rr-medium. 2) Observe initial TLS handshake duration and edge routing chosen (edge-proxy logs). 3) Reproduce by issuing many short-lived streaming requests concurrently (~200/s) to trigger connection churn. 4) Correlate chosen POP in edge-proxy logs and TLS handshake metrics.

Note: Reproduction is probabilistic; load patterns that cause SNI cache evictions increase probability.
logs: Edge-proxy logs show repeated TLS handshake start -> SNI resolve -> upstream choice eu-west-pop -> TCP/TLS handshake complete -> request forwarded. Timestamp samples: 2026-03-12T02:12:03Z handshake 340ms, upstream eu-west-pop chosen; following requests show 320-560ms for handshake when routed remote. No upstream 5xx in serving runtime logs. Kernel-level retransmits seen in network telemetry for cross-region connections. Sample log references: edge-proxy: session=abcd-1234 sni=atlasmail.prod host=api.atlasmail.com chosen_pop=eu-west-pop tls_time_ms=410 trace_id=xyz; routing: route_decision=miss reason=SNI_CACHE_MISS.
metrics_summary:
- p50 token latency: +20ms (stable)
- p95 token latency: +80ms (small bump)
- p99 token latency: +4200ms correlated with cross-region upstream selection
- TLS handshake latency (edge): median 45ms, but tail shows spikes 300-600ms on impacted requests
- connection churn rate increased by 35% for AtlasMail between 2026-03-12 02:00 and 04:00 UTC
- no CPU/GPU saturation on serving nodes; network egress rates show increased inter-region bandwidth usage
investigation_notes:
- Initial triage: routing decision path shows SNI-to-POP affinity lookup returned miss for a subset of AtlasMail requests. When SNI cache misses occur we fall back to remote POP selection that prefers eu-west for reasons tied to a stale anycast route table entry.
- Observed correlation between high connection churn (many short sessions) and SNI cache eviction frequency in the edge-proxy process. SNI cache eviction caused by LRU under bursty connect patterns.
- Remote selection path increases TLS handshake RTT due to cross-region RTT and occasional BGP path asymmetry.
- No certificate validation errors; TLS completes successfully but costs additional 300-500ms per request.
- Hypothesis 1: SNI cache capacity and eviction policy is too small for high-churn customers leading to repeated remote POP selection.
- Hypothesis 2: Control plane routing table for some prefixes was stale causing preference of eu-west POP despite edge affinity; seen in one routing controller refresh window.
- Temporary workaround applied: pinned AtlasMail account to local POP via edge routing policy (applied 2026-03-13 07:10 UTC) which reduced cross-region handshakes by ~92% for subsequent traffic samples.
- Collected traces (edge + serving) and exported to support bucket: s3://redwood-support/sup-98177/traces/
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) - 2026-03-12: Customer reported intermittent long-tail streaming delays. Asked for request ids and sample timestamps.
AtlasMail (Customer) - 2026-03-12: Provided sample trace ids and stated impact on client sessions; provided rates and token counts.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Initial check shows repeated SNI cache misses in edge-proxy. Started deeper tracing and BGP path checks.

Rhea Singh (Routing) - 2026-03-13: Found control-plane refresh that overlapped with customer traffic and a route weight change that temporarily favored remote POP for some prefixes. Investigating fix and guardrails.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) - 2026-03-13: Applied temporary account-level POP pin for AtlasMail; monitoring after change shows p99s returning near baseline.
Product (Edge) - 2026-03-14: Proposed changes to SNI cache sizing and TTL heuristics for high-churn customers.
resolution_notes:
Workaround: Pinned AtlasMail to nearest POP (us-west) to avoid SNI cache miss path. This reduced observed p99 token latency by ~92% for their traffic.

Planned next steps:
- Short-term (by 2026-03-18): Increase edge-proxy SNI cache capacity and adjust eviction TTL for high-churn traffic; add telemetry to count SNI cache misses per account.
- Medium-term (by 2026-03-30): Add control-plane guard to prevent routing refreshes from changing POP preference for recently-seen customer prefixes without a staggered rollout; add a canary window.
- Follow-up: Run post-mortem on control-plane refresh overlap and update runbook (link to Confluence page).

Status: Mitigated for AtlasMail via pinning. Engineering changes planned and prioritized.
